# <span id="aanchor124"></span> Exception Resolver

[Overview](Exception%20Resolver.md) \| <a href="#" class="selected">Exception Grid</a> \| [Object Explorer](Exception%20Resolver_Object%20Explorer.md) \| [Notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md) \| [Settings](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md)

## Exception Grid

The exception grid displays all of the exceptions that meet the filter parameters that you have specified. Several options are available for sorting, organizing and managing exceptions.

If you double-click a location exception in the exception resolver, the Balance Explorer will open and will be preset with the following:

- Object Selector = Location
- Location Number = Location that the exception was generated for
- Date Range = Contract Month
- From = Month/Year of exception
- To = Month immediately following the month of exception



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 903;height: 496;" />

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Columns">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Grid Columns</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Columns">

The following columns are available in the exception grid:

- **Device Number** - Numeric identifier assigned to the object when it was created in the application (example: meter number).

- **Device Name** - Identifier assigned to the object when it was created in the application (for example, meter name).

- **Effective Date** - Date or date range associated with the exception data.

- **Generated Date** - Date or date range when the exception was initially generated.

- **Description** - Actual exception text explaining the issue and cause.

- **Exception Number** - Unique numeric identifier associated with the exception.

- **Exception Count** - Total number of exceptions in the group (summary rows only). (See: [Grouping Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Grouping))

- **Edit Reason\*** - The reason given for changing the exception status.

- **Edit Code\*** - The numeric code associated with the edit reason.

- **Comment\*** - Additional information regarding changes to an exception status.

  \* These items are required if the Require Edit Reasons for Exceptions option is enabled under **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **System** \> **System Configuration**.

- **Field Value** - Data value that the validation process tested against.

- **Alarm Level** - Value limit defined for the data.

- **Status** - Current status of the exception (example: Unresolved).

- **Type** - Type of device or object (defined under **Object Types**).

- **Severity** - Priority level defined for the exception. Modify severity levels in the [Exception Description Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Exception%20Description%20Editor.md).

- **Modified By** - User ID that last modified the status of the exception.

- **Modified Date** - Date when the exception status was last modified.

- **Field Name** - Name of the database field that contains the flagged data (example: Temperature).

- **Table Name** - Name of the database table that contains the flagged data (example: FC_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES).

- **Machine** - Name of the computer that last accessed the data.

- **User Name** - User ID that last accessed the data.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Column Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Column Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Column Options">

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options:

- **Full Expand** - Expands all exception groups.

- **Full Collapse** - Collapses all exception groups.

- **Sort Ascending** - Sorts exceptions by the selected column in ascending order.

- **Sort Descending** - Sorts exceptions by the selected column in descending order.

- **Show Column Chooser** - Opens the Column Selector so that you can select which columns display on the grid. (See: [Column Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector))

  Easily remove a column by dragging and dropping the column header outside of the grid. FLOWCAL retains changes that you make from the grid until you close the Exception Resolver. Use the [Column Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector) to save a column layout.

- **Best Fit** - Expands the selected column to completely display the contents.

- **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expands all columns to completely display the contents.

- **Filter Editor** - Launches the Filter Editor so that you can create conditional statements. The statements can include any column or value within the column.

<br/>![](data:image/png;base64,)

##### Column Order

To change the column order, click a column header and drag and drop the column to the new location.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Sorting">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Sorting Exceptions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Sorting">

By default, FLOWCAL groups and sorts exceptions by device number, then exception description, and then status.

To sort exceptions by an individual column, click the column header or the up/down arrow in the header. The arrow might be hidden because of column width.

You can only sort columns within the grouping order. For example, if the grouping order in Settings is device number, description, and status, then status will only be sorted ascending/descending with a specific device number and exception description. To sort by number and then status, in the Group Selector, device number must be at the top, followed by status.

Sorting by exception count applies to groups only—not individual exceptions. If you click the **Exception Count** column heading, FLOWCAL sorts the summary rows (groups) by the number of exceptions they contain.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Filtering">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Filtering Exceptions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Filtering">

You can filter exceptions by a single column or by multiple columns.

<div class="procedure">

To filter by a single column:

1.  To display the filter icon, hover over a column header.
2.  To open the Filter dialog box, click the filter icon. The box contains two tabs:

> - **Filter Values** - Select the values you want to display.
> - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example, "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). First select a condition, and then specify a value.

1.  To close the Filter dialog box, click on the grid. After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter.

To filter using multiple columns, right-click on a column header and select **Filter Editor**.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Grouping">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Grouping Exceptions</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Grouping">

By default, FLOWCAL groups exceptions by device number, exception description, and status.

A summary (or group) row includes the device number, device name, effective date range, exception description, exception number, exception count, and status. (See: [Grouping Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Grouping))

You cannot update exceptions in bulk by selecting a group. To update multiple exceptions, expand the group and then select the exceptions individually, or press **Ctrl+A**.

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Other Options">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Other Menu Options</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Other Options">

Right-click an exception or group of exceptions to access the following options:

- **Add Notes** - Write [notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md) for objects associated with an exception.

- **View Notes** - View [notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md) for objects associated with an exception.

- **Email** - Open the email dialog box so that you can populate the email with the selected exceptions.

- **Reschedule Sample** - Reschedule samples for Source Analysis exceptions (TESTit 2 Integrated users only).

  To use this feature, you must enable the **Allow Reschedule of Analysis Samples** option (**Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **System** \> **System Configuration**).

</div>
